en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga,
Pācittiya Section
The Chapter on Pregnant Women 61. The Training Rule on Pregnant Women.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, nuns were ordaining women who were pregnant.
She went about for alms,
and people said this:
“Alms for the noble lady; the noble lady is heavily burdened.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying, “How can these bhikkhunīs give the full admission to a pregnant woman?”
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were modest … [as above] … grumbled, complained, and criticized:
“How can these bhikkhunīs give the full admission to a pregnant woman? … [as above] …
“Is it true, monks, that nuns are ordaining pregnant women?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs ordain a woman who is pregnant?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faithful...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: 'If a bhikkhunī should ordain a woman who is pregnant, that is an offense of wrong-doing.'"
“Whatever nun, however, should ordain a pregnant woman, it is an offense entailing expiation.
Regarding “whatever nun”: whichever nun of such a kind... [as before]...
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Pregnant" means:
"One who has conceived a fetus" is what is meant.
"Should ordain" means she should confer full admission.
If, thinking, “I will ordain her,” she seeks out a group, a preceptor, a bowl, or a robe; or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the motion (ñatti), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
For two proclamations (kammavācā), there are offenses of wrong-doing.
At the conclusion of the formal act (*kammavācā*), there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for the preceptor;
there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*) for the assembly and for the instructor.
If she ordains one who is pregnant while perceiving her as being pregnant, there is an offense of expiation.
If she ordains one who is pregnant while being in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she ordains one who is pregnant while perceiving her as not pregnant, there is no offense.
If she ordains one who is not pregnant while perceiving her as pregnant, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she is not pregnant but she is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she is not pregnant and she perceives her as not pregnant, there is no offense.
There is no offense—
If one ordains a pregnant woman perceiving her as not pregnant;
if one ordains a non-pregnant woman perceiving her as not pregnant; [or] in the case of a madwoman.
"For one who is a first offender.
The first training rule is concluded.
